title: Cheapest first
prompt: Show the title and price of every book, from cheapest to most expensive. Replace the ___.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM books; INSERT INTO books VALUES (10, 'Copper Moon', 'Ada Hill', 'Fantasy', 20.0, 100, 2020), (11, 'North Light', 'Raj Dev', 'Travel', 7.5, 180, 2015), (12, 'Sky Atlas', 'Ada Hill', 'Science', 25.0, 300, 2023);

solutions: SELECT title, price FROM books ORDER BY price;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT title, price FROM books ORDER BY price DESC;
SELECT title, price FROM books ORDER BY title;

title: Highest paid first
prompt: Show each employee's name and salary, highest salary first. Break ties alphabetically by name.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC, name;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary, name;
SELECT name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY name, salary DESC;

title: Top three
prompt: Show the title and pages of the three longest books, longest first.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM books; INSERT INTO books VALUES (10, 'Copper Moon', 'Ada Hill', 'Fantasy', 20.0, 100, 2020), (11, 'North Light', 'Raj Dev', 'Travel', 7.5, 180, 2015), (12, 'Sky Atlas', 'Ada Hill', 'Science', 25.0, 300, 2023);

solutions: SELECT title, pages FROM books ORDER BY pages DESC LIMIT 3;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT title, pages FROM books LIMIT 3;
SELECT title, pages FROM books ORDER BY pages LIMIT 3;

title: Latest reading
prompt: Show the city, reading_date, and temp_c of the single most recent reading. If several share that date, take the one with the highest id.
hints: Sort by date descending, then id descending.
solutions: SELECT city, reading_date, temp_c FROM readings ORDER BY reading_date DESC, id DESC LIMIT 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT city, reading_date, temp_c FROM readings ORDER BY reading_date LIMIT 1;
SELECT city, reading_date, temp_c FROM readings ORDER BY reading_date DESC LIMIT 2;

title: Second highest
prompt: Show the second-highest different salary, in a column named salary.
hints: Remove duplicates, sort, then use OFFSET.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET salary = 90000 WHERE id = 12;

solutions: SELECT DISTINCT salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;
wrongSolutions.why: A tie can repeat the highest salary

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT DISTINCT salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1;

title: Fix the clause order
prompt: This should show the two most expensive products with their price, but it fails. Fix it.
starterSql:
SELECT name, price
FROM products
LIMIT 2
ORDER BY price DESC;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 2;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, price FROM products LIMIT 2;
SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price LIMIT 2;

title: Grouped listing
prompt: Show the category, name, and price of every product. Sort by category A to Z, then by price from highest to lowest within each category.
hints: Each sort column can have its own direction.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT category, name, price FROM products ORDER BY category, price DESC;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT category, name, price FROM products ORDER BY category DESC, price DESC;
SELECT category, name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC, category;

title: Recent hires in a department
prompt: Show the name and hire_date of the two most recently hired employees in department 2.
hints: Filter first, then sort and limit.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET department_id = 2 WHERE id IN (11, 13, 15);

solutions: SELECT name, hire_date FROM employees WHERE department_id = 2 ORDER BY hire_date DESC LIMIT 2;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, hire_date FROM employees ORDER BY hire_date DESC LIMIT 2;
SELECT name, hire_date FROM employees WHERE department_id = 2 ORDER BY hire_date LIMIT 2;
